svg.title: A streaming platform for 100 million viewers: complete AWS architecture
svg.desc: Three paths: live and VOD media through CloudFront to players; regional ALB to Spring Boot on EKS and three data stores; Go ingestion through Kinesis to consumers and S3. Cognito, DRM, WAF, security, delivery and observability support these paths. Repeat regional cells with tested failover capacity.

g.text: THE WHOLE SYSTEM, IN ONE VIEW
Proposed architecture • 200 Tbps at 2 Mbps/viewer • 25M video-segment requests/s at 4-second segments
Solid teal arrows show media delivery. Players request cached objects directly from the CDN.
a second provider is not drawn here.
Logical serving cell: ALB ingress; private EKS workloads across AZs; managed data services. Repeat by cohort and region.
API responses return playback URLs and authorization; video bytes never pass through these services.
Dashed arrows: player identity/license exchanges and WAF attachment. API data arrows: logical access, responses omitted.
Same player → regional ALB ingress, then an independent ingestion workload. Example: 3.33M heartbeat events/s.
Cross-cutting services, not a sequential request path. Scope permissions and capacity to each workload.
REPEAT TESTED CELLS • RESERVE FAILOVER CAPACITY • PRE-SCALE BEFORE THE EVENT
Secondary paths: SQS workers for retryable jobs; outbox events update entitlement projections; progress consumers write DynamoDB.
One icon represents a logical role, not one global instance. DNS is endpoint selection, not an HTTP proxy. DR and return paths are simplified.
Official AWS Architecture Icons, July 2026. Independent educational design; no AWS endorsement or measured 100M-viewer claim.
